subject: zoology_2
question_text: Name the keystone bone of the cranium. Where is it located?

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.50, VSAQ 81. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The bone
steps.why: It is called the keystone because it touches almost every other cranial bone and locks them together.
common_mistakes: Naming the frontal or occipital bone.
Spelling it sphenoid but placing it in the face.
steps.memory_tip: The keystone in an arch is the one every other stone leans on.
lines: The sphenoid bone is the keystone bone of

steps.label: Where it lies
steps.why: Lying at the base, it can reach every surrounding bone at once.
common_mistakes: Placing it at the top of the skull. It lies at the base.
steps.memory_tip: At the base of the cranium, touching most of the others.
lines: It lies in the base of the cranium.

lines.text: It touches most of the other cranial bones

insider_note: Two questions in one line: the name and the place. Answer both or lose half the marks.
